commits.subject: chore(horizon): record the transport leaf and the witness-form obstruction
commits.summary: Adds the pull-transport leaf (the composability hinge) and notes the concurrent duplication of the (c1) converse, filed to human as a coordination issue.

commits.subject: picard: the chart obstruction in witness form; drop my duplicate of the (c1) converse
commits.summary:
**Deduplicated.** Another team proved the same (c1)-forces-leak-freeness keystone by the same route concurrently (DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean), and theirs is richer (an iff, plus the composed verdict). I removed my DivSchemeCertZarConverse.lean rather than keep two proofs of one fact.

**What is new.** not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses: the obstruction with two witness points, one off each pinned chart — the form in which a concrete divisor (fibre $\{0,\infty\}$) refutes certifiability, with no leak hypothesis.

commits.subject: picard: (c1) forces leak-freeness — the converse the chart verdict rested on
commits.summary:
**Keystone.** Certificate clause (c1) was asserted everywhere to force leak-freeness but proved nowhere. Now proved: finiteness of the colength makes Spec of it finite over Spec R hence universally closed, and SEPARATEDNESS of the ambient cancels it to a closed map into the curve, whose image is the piece trace.

**Effect.** IsCertified.forall_supportLeak_eq_empty makes the chart-confinement verdict a statement about IsCertified itself, not merely about one sufficient-condition assembler. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

commits.subject: picard: state the honest leak/clopen equivalence and fix the idempotent bricks' namespace
commits.summary:
**Overclaim corrected.** The two directions were not formal converses (one concluded IsClopen, the other assumed only IsClosed). The content is now an explicit Iff on the closedness half, with the openness half recorded separately as the unconditional free rider it is.

**Namespace.** The idempotent bricks are statements about modules, so they were resolving wrongly as AlgebraicGeometry.Module.…; they now live in the root namespace as intended.

commits.subject: picard: the pullback transport of support and unit loci
commits.summary:
**The hinge.** supportLocus (E.pullback f) = f.base preimage of supportLocus, both inclusions from stalkMap being a LOCAL ring hom (so it preserves AND reflects unit-ness), with the germ of a pulled equation being the stalkMap image of the original germ.

**Why it was needed.** Every support/no-leak/clopen lemma of the lane is stated on relCurve C R, while the pointwise gate consumes the PULLED system over an Away chart; without this transport none of them could compose with the gate.

commits.subject: chore(roadmap): itemize the last link and flag its circularity trap
commits.summary: **Five steps, one open.** The equalizer algebra already exists (gluedSubalgebra); the idempotent-to-summand and clopen-to-(c1) steps landed this session; only the packet decomposition remains — and it must come from the geometry of $Z$ finite over the base, not from $W(d)$ own clause (c2), which would be circular.

commits.subject: chore(horizon): task comment for the round-6 certificate reframing
commits.summary: Records the two proved no-gos, the Z-clopen identification, the idempotent brick, and the build-reachability fix.

commits.subject: chore(horizon): record the clopen identification and the build-reachability fix
commits.summary: **Lane state.** No-leak identified with the Z-clopen principle; the idempotent brick landed; the only outstanding link is production of the clopen packet (I-0209 W-as-algebra extraction).

commits.subject: picard: (c1) from a clopen piece trace, with no fibre containment
commits.summary:
**Chain assembled.** A clopen piece trace gives no-leak, hence Module.Finite of the colength; with fibrewise regularity (landed for seed adaptations) that is the entire (c1) input. So under the Z-clopen hypothesis the certificate finiteness side needs no fibre analysis and no Cech-cokernel flatness.

**What is left.** Only the PRODUCTION of the clopen trace — I-0209 W-as-algebra extraction. PrimeSpectrum.isClopen_iff_zeroLocus and exists_idempotent_basicOpen_eq_of_isClopen are the mathlib translations connecting a clopen packet to the idempotent the landed brick consumes.

commits.subject: picard: flat companion of the idempotent brick, matching the DD-R pieces
commits.summary: **The applicable form.** Piece section rings are known FLAT over $R$ (localizations of the free pinned-chart rings), not projective, so it is the flat retract version that discharges the (c1) input from a packet idempotent.

commits.subject: picard: land the idempotent brick — clopen packets give projective colengths for free
commits.summary: **Direct summand.** For idempotent $e$, multiplication by $e$ is a well-defined $R$-linear section of $B \to B/(1-e)$, so the quotient is a retract of $B$ and inherits projectivity with NO flatness or finiteness input — the algebraic core of the packet-splitting construction I-0209 asked for.

commits.subject: picard: identify the assembler's no-leak clause with the Z-clopen principle
commits.summary:
**Same condition.** The piece trace $\mathrm{supp} \cap U$ is always OPEN in the subspace $\mathrm{supp}$, so it is clopen there exactly when it is closed in $X$ — exactly when the leak locus is empty. So the assembler no-leak clause and the recorded Z-clopen certificate principle (I-0209) are literally the same statement, proved both ways.

**Consequence for the lane.** The certificate finiteness obligation was never really fibrewise: it asks that the piece trace be a clopen part of the divisor scheme. That reframes the remaining work and explains why fibre analyses kept not closing it.

commits.subject: picard: no-leak over a shrunken base with no fibre analysis, and wire the Zar tower into the default build
commits.summary:
**No-leak for free on a dense open.** The leak locus is closed and its base image is closed under the properness licence, so over the open complement nothing leaks; refining to a basic open gives the Localization.Away shape the pointwise gate consumes. The remaining fibre work is confined to base points INSIDE that closed image.

**Build gap fixed.** The whole DivSchemeCertZar* tower (5 files from earlier sessions) was unreachable from the root module, so plain `lake build` never checked it; one import now pulls it in (9043 -> 9071 jobs, green).

commits.subject: picard: refute the tube-fibre leaf's one-piece shape for supports meeting both charts
commits.summary: **Corollary.** not_exists_unique_support_piece: no adaptation can have at most one support-meeting piece once a support point lies in $V_0 \cap V_1$ — the two charts partitions force one piece each. This refutes the shape the tube-fibre leaf was aiming at, independently of how the cover is refined.

commits.subject: chore(horizon): record the separated-adaptation no-go in the certificate lane
commits.summary: **Bounded from two sides.** The certificate packaging now has two proved no-gos: a cleverer submodule is ruled out by the syzygy equivalence, a cleverer choice of pieces by supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated.

commits.subject: picard: prove the separated route's no-go, confining it to fibre-supported systems
commits.summary:
**No-go.** Both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a support point in $V_0 \cap V_1$ lies in a piece of EACH chart; both germs are non-units, so that off-diagonal overlap ideal is proper and separation fails. Separation is therefore available only when the support avoids the chart overlap.

**Consequence.** isCertified_of_separated is a correct certificate route but applies only to fibre-confined divisors, not a general degree-$g$ system — so the flat-cokernel content of DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy is not evaded. The scope is now a theorem, not a prose caveat.

commits.subject: picard: reduce separation to one support-meeting piece
commits.summary: **Geometric criterion.** An overlap disjoint from the support carries a unit equation, so its overlap colength vanishes; hence an adaptation in which at most one piece meets the support is automatically separated, and the certificate needs only (c1) plus a rank sum.

commits.subject: picard: certify a support-separated adaptation with no kernel-spanning input
commits.summary:
**Reduction.** For an adaptation whose off-diagonal overlap colengths vanish, the Cech difference is literally zero: the equalizer is the whole product $\prod_j \mathrm{colength}(j)$, so both flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) are free and no kernel-spanning submodule is needed.

**Why it unblocks.** The pointwise gate accepts ANY adaptation over the shrunken base, so separation may be arranged geometrically by the tube; the previously obstructed fibrewise flatness over a nonreduced base is discharged rather than evaded.
